brief: A Market Ear roundup argues the conventional read on Wednesday's FOMC, that a Fed hike sells off bonds, may be inverted this cycle. The 10-year hit 5.03 percent, highest since 2007, after oil and inflation concerns forced a hawkish repricing of the Fed. Goldman shifted to expecting a September hike despite seeing little fundamental justification. BofA argues a hold, not a hike, would force investors to demand a larger inflation and credibility premium at the long end, since higher short rates now can mean less term premium later. The front end has already sold off more than the long end, 2-year yield up 22bp versus 10-year up 14bp from September 9 to 14, flattening 2s10s to 32bp. Deutsche Banks positioning measure sits near the 5th percentile, a bearish extreme, and large CTA convexity means a yield reversal could force momentum funds to cover shorts. Deutsche Bank historical work counters this: 10-year yields have typically risen roughly 114bp in the year after a tightening cycle starts. The note holds both can be true, structurally bearish but tactically rally-prone, and sets 4.81 and 4.73 percent as reversal levels and 5.15 to 5.20 percent as the zone that would invalidate the bond-friendly thesis.
